title: AI Agent Security: Best Practices for Safe Tool-Calling
summary: Function calling allows automated systems to interact with external software securely. You will identify common injection risks and implement validation.
body_markdown:
## Sandboxing execution environments with Activepieces


Activepieces provides a managed orchestration layer that prevents an LLM from executing code directly on your production servers by routing every tool-call through a decoupled, sandboxed environment.


The MIT-licensed core provides access to **732 integrations** , where every action is defined in the Integrations Framework to ensure the LLM only interacts with validated schemas.


By checking the open source repository, security teams can verify that the same code running a deterministic flow step is what is exposed as an MCP tool, preventing the model from bypassing established security boundaries.


### Running tool-calls in ephemeral Docker containers


Isolation is achieved by wrapping every automation step in a discrete Docker container that exists only for the duration of that specific task. Because these containers are ephemeral, any malicious code executed by a compromised agent lacks a persistent filesystem to hide in.


This architecture forces a "clean slate" for every interaction.


### Separating LLM reasoning from connector execution logic


The platform functions as a secure gateway by strictly separating the LLM’s reasoning process from the actual execution of connector logic.


The LLM Kernel generates the intent and parameters but has no direct network access to the target API. The Integration Connector is a pre-defined code block that receives parameters, validates them, and performs the API call within the sandbox.


The Execution Bridge is the only communication channel allowed between the two, ensuring the model never sees underlying credentials.


### Monitoring and logging tool-call telemetry for forensic audits


Centralizing these calls creates a comprehensive audit trail. Every decision an agent makes is captured in the Run Details and Debugging UI, providing a step-by-step trace of the tool-call.


This allows you to distinguish between a model hallucinating a bad command and a deliberate prompt injection attack.


Every agent tool call and the data it acted on is traced alongside the deterministic flow steps running next to it.


MoneyGram and Moneypenny run Activepieces in production, where these traces export as audit logs and event streams into the SIEM their security teams already run, ensuring agent decisions are reviewed with the same rigor as manual workflow steps.
